name: localStorage
plain: A browser store of up to about 5 MB per site that scripts read at any time and that survives restarts.
meaning: Holds settings, drafts, and very often a tracker's visitor ID that is re-created if the cookie is deleted. It is not sent to servers on its own, but every script on the page can read it. A common 'respawn' source for IDs.

access.persistence: Until cleared by user or evicted. Safari deletes script written storage after 7 days of Safari use without a user visit
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can keep up to about 5 MB of text notes per site, until cleared
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens as you use the site or change settings.
can: Remember settings, drafts and sign in tokens
Keep them after you restart the browser
Use them again on every visit
cannot: Keep them after you clear site data or close a private window
Keep them in Safari after 7 days of use without a visit
limits.differs: Safari may delete it after 7 days of use without a visit. Chrome and Firefox do not.

story.what_it_is: A store of up to about 5 MB per site that scripts can read any time and that survives restarts.

marketing.name: Web Storage API
marketing.pitch: Documents how sites save small amounts of data in the browser for later visits.

story.for_you: You never see it. It is why a site remembers your dark mode, your last search or your game score the next time you come back.
story.for_makers: It is the easiest way to keep small settings, so it is everywhere. It is also a place where trackers store IDs, because it survives restarts and any script on the page can read it.

use_cases.example: A word game or puzzle keeps your streak and best score here.
A to do list app remembers your tasks without needing an account.
A store remembers the items you recently viewed.
A social site remembers a draft post that you did not send.
A tracking script stores a visitor ID and your last ad click here.
A site analytics script keeps a session ID here to link visits together.
A learning site remembers where you stopped in a lesson.

technical_bounds: About 5 MiB per origin in Chrome, Firefox and Safari
Synchronous API blocks the main thread
Not shared across origins or (3P) partitions
No expiry set by the API

legit_uses: User settings, offline drafts, feature flags
abuse: Respawning tracking IDs after cookie deletion

history.change: ITP 7 day cap on script writable storage applied to localStorage
Third party localStorage partitioned by top level site
Total Cookie Protection partitions it for all users
